title: Unified Global Inventory Registry
business: A multinational retail logistics firm managing regional warehouses.
problem: Discrepancies between regional databases caused stock-outs and redundant procurement because no single system held the authoritative count for high-value assets.
solution: Implementing a Single Source of Truth (SSOT) pattern where a centralized registry service acts as the exclusive authoritative representation for item availability, forcing all regional systems to read from and write to this central node rather than maintaining local state.
steps: Identify the canonical data entity representing the physical asset state.
Deprecate local write permissions in regional databases to prevent data divergence.
Expose a centralized API layer that enforces validation rules before updating the master registry.
Implement a read-through cache strategy to maintain performance without sacrificing the authoritative nature of the registry.
outcome: Consistent inventory visibility across all regions, eliminating conflicting reports and enabling reliable automated replenishment.
limitation: The centralized registry introduces a potential latency bottleneck and a single point of failure; monitoring can be performed by tracking the request-to-response time latency metrics of the registry API.

questions.question: In Unified Global Inventory Registry, what is the primary reason for adopting a Single Source of Truth?
options: To resolve discrepancies between regional databases and prevent stock-outs.
To increase the number of regional databases for redundancy.
To allow regional systems to maintain their own independent inventory counts.
To improve the aesthetic design of the inventory dashboard.
questions.explanation: The scenario identifies that regional discrepancies caused operational failures, which the SSOT pattern addresses by centralizing authority.
questions.evidence: Discrepancies between regional databases caused stock-outs and redundant procurement because no single system held the authoritative count for high-value assets.

questions.question: In Unified Global Inventory Registry, what is a significant trade-off of the proposed architecture?
options: It makes the system impossible to scale horizontally.
It creates a single point of failure and potential latency bottleneck.
It requires all regional systems to be offline during updates.
It eliminates the need for any audit logging.
questions.explanation: Centralizing data creates a dependency on a single node, which introduces risks regarding availability and performance.
questions.evidence: The centralized registry introduces a potential latency bottleneck and a single point of failure; monitoring can be performed by tracking the request-to-response time latency metrics of the registry API.
